```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

ailogR logs AI use one task at a time. Entries go in two CSV files in an
`ai-use/` folder: `ai_log.csv`, one row per task, and `ai_tools.csv`, one
row per tool and model version.

```{r}
library(ailogR)
project <- file.path(tempdir(), "stream-temperature")
create_ai_log(project)
```

Here `project` is a temporary folder; in your own work, run
`create_ai_log()` from the project's root.

## Logging in the console

Most of the time you run `log_ai()` with no arguments at the end of a work
session. It asks up to six questions, listing the tool and research stage you
used last as option 1:

```
> log_ai()
AI tool:
1: claude-opus-5.5
2: Add a new tool
Selection: 1
Research stage:
1: software
2: conceptualization
...
Selection: 1
Task, in one line: Function to import HOBO logger files
If the AI output were subtly wrong, would that show?
1: obvious: you can read and judge all of it (text edits, comments)
2: checkable: a wrong output would fail or look wrong (plots, file import)
3: silent: a wrong output would still run and look plausible (joins, models, unit conversions)
Selection: 2
How did you check it, and what did it show? Ran on 3 real files; errors on a malformed one
What did you decide or change? Chose column names and time zone handling
Logged row 1: Function to import HOBO logger files (checkable, accepted).
```

The question about how you checked it is skipped for `obvious` uses. The
first time, choose "Add a new tool" and answer four questions about the
tool. `vignette("what-to-log")` explains when to log and how to choose
between `obvious`, `checkable` and `silent`.

## Logging with arguments

Every question is also an argument, which is how scripts and AI tools log:

```{r}
add_ai_tool("Claude", "Anthropic", "Opus 5.5", access_mode = "web", path = project)

log_ai("Function to import HOBO logger files",
       tool_id = "claude-opus-5.5", research_stage = "software",
       error_visibility = "checkable",
       how_checked = "Ran on 3 real files; errors on a malformed one",
       human_decisions = "Chose column names and time zone handling",
       path = project)

log_ai("Convert logger pressure to water depth",
       tool_id = "claude-opus-5.5", research_stage = "data_curation",
       error_visibility = "silent",
       how_checked = "Matched staff gauge readings within 1 cm on 12 visits",
       human_decisions = "Chose the barometric correction and water density",
       evidence = "R/depth.R; tests/test-depth.R",
       path = project)
```

An entry with a missing or invalid field is not saved, and the error says
which field to fix.

## Checking and editing

```{r}
check_ai_log(project)
```

To change an entry, give its row number and the new values. Run
interactively with no values, `edit_ai_log()` lets you pick the entry and
the fields.

```{r}
edit_ai_log(2, outcome = "modified", path = project)
```

## Drafting a statement

```{r}
draft_ai_statement(project)
```

The draft is a starting point: edit it to say what matters for your work and
fill in the bracketed text.

## Using AI as a method

If AI itself produced data or results, such as extracting values from papers
or classifying images, log it with `ai_role = "method"`. Those entries also
need `how_checked` and `prompt_archive`, and the statement describes them
separately. Archive enough for someone else to repeat the work: the prompts,
the model version and settings, and the inputs.

```{r}
log_ai("Extract litter mass loss and incubation days from 120 papers",
       tool_id = "claude-opus-5.5", research_stage = "data_curation",
       ai_role = "method", error_visibility = "silent",
       how_checked = "Compared with hand extraction for 30 papers: 2 of 410 values differed",
       prompt_archive = "extraction/prompts/",
       human_decisions = "Defined the fields and the rules for ambiguous tables",
       path = project)
```

## Letting AI tools draft entries

AI tools can draft entries for you to review; see
`vignette("ai-drafted-entries")`.
